gloss: to shine down intensely; to beat down (of the sun)

forms.label: ている past polite
forms.negative: {照|て}りつけていませんでした

definitions.gloss: to shine down intensely; to beat down; to blaze down
definitions.explanation: Describes the sun shining fiercely and relentlessly, creating intense heat. Conveys the oppressive, punishing quality of strong sunlight.

examples.japanese: {太陽|たいよう}が{照|て}りつけている。
{真夏|まなつ}の{日差|ひざ}しが{容赦|ようしゃ}なく{照|て}りつけていた。
examples.english: The midsummer sun was shining down mercilessly.

examples.japanese: {炎天下|えんてんか}で{太陽|たいよう}に{照|て}りつけられながら、{工事|こうじ}{現場|げんば}で{働|はたら}いている{人|ひと}たちがいる。
examples.english: There are people working at construction sites under the blazing sun.

notes:
A vivid weather verb that specifically describes the sun bearing down with intense, oppressive heat. Almost exclusively used with {太陽|たいよう} or {日差|ひざ}し as the subject. Strongly associated with summer heat and often appears in descriptions of {猛暑|もうしょ} (extreme heat).

USAGE:
The progressive form {照|て}りつけている is the most common, describing ongoing fierce sunlight. The passive {照|て}りつけられる emphasizes the discomfort experienced by the person under the sun.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {太陽|たいよう}が{照|て}りつける — the sun beats down
- {日差|ひざ}しが{照|て}りつける — the sunlight blazes down
- {照|て}りつける{暑|あつ}さ — scorching heat

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {照|て}りつく — similar meaning but less common; same nuance of relentless sunlight
- {降|ふ}り{注|そそ}ぐ — to pour down; used for both sunlight and rain, more neutral
- {照|て}る — to shine; basic verb without the intensity or oppressive nuance
